from there its powers, namely for expelling, are rendered stronger, and moreover the doses of precipitated mercury <note>original: "Mercurij præcipitati"</note> may be more easily formed for administering or swallowing, specifically in the form of pills. This precipitated mercury is therefore uniquely praised and recommended, and indeed it performs very well. The same is achieved by the Mercury of Life <term>Mercurius vitæ</term> <gloss>antimony oxychloride, an emetic and purgative</gloss> or the Flowers of the Butter of Antimony <term>flores butyri antimonij</term>, of which we spoke above, if four to twelve grains of it are administered for three full days in an extract of Hellebore and Bitter Apple <term>colocynthidis</term> <gloss>Citrullus colocynthis, a potent laxative</gloss>; it certainly expels the dissolved salt successfully. But afterwards, sweating and urination should be provoked with a decoction of sarsaparilla, Holy Wood <term>ligni sancti</term> <gloss>Guaiacum resin, used for its medicinal heat</gloss>, or asarabacca root <term>radice asari</term>, always adding the Spirit of Tartar <term>spiritu Tartari</term> <gloss>an acidic distillate of potassium bitartrate</gloss>, or other diaphoretics <note>remedies to induce sweating</note> and diuretics <note>remedies to increase urination</note> mentioned above. Especially, however, by adding the secret essence <term>arcano</term> of wormwood or Blessed Thistle <term>cardui benedicti</term>. Here it must be noted, however, that the administration of the Mercury of Life for three days often tends to cause a prolapse of the anus in adults, which is afterwards rarely, or rather with difficulty, cured. In treating dropsy <term>hydrope</term> <gloss>edema or swelling from fluid retention</gloss>, it is necessary that such purgatives be used right from the beginning of the treatment; afterwards, diuretics and water-expelling remedies <term>hydrotica</term> should follow. Otherwise, surely the "latter before the former" <term>ὕστερον πρότερον</term> <gloss>hysteron proteron; a reversal of the natural or logical order</gloss> would be practiced here: all the serum or water would be driven down to the kidneys and ureters, where afterwards, because of the heavy burden, very persistent symptoms often tend to arise. Furthermore, in the preparation of the extract of Black Hellebore root <term>Hellebori nigri</term>, it is safer to use the wine itself instead of Spirit of Wine <note>high-proof distilled alcohol</note>; the root itself should only boil gently and quietly with it, and this must be done with fresh wine until all the essential power has been extracted from the roots; afterwards, the extract is to be reduced to the thickness of honey by evaporation or distillation. For the Spirit of Wine, on account of those things in which it is more powerful in its sulfurous principle <note>the flammable or oily essence of a substance in alchemy</note> rather than its liquid part

<summary>This page details the administration of mercury and antimony compounds to treat dropsy, warning that purgatives must be used before diuretics to avoid overwhelming the kidneys. It also provides instructions for extracting the medicinal properties of Black Hellebore using a gentle wine-based boil.</summary>
